title.label: Paid for a notetaker, got a sales funnel

content.label: I paid for this app to take notes, not to dismiss pop-ups. Every few sessions, another prompt interrupts my work to push a new service or subscription feature. The latest one is worse: without asking me, the app scheduled my notes to move from iCloud to Notability's own servers on a fixed date, and my only choices are Update now or Postpone. After the move, iCloud sync no longer works, even though this very App Store page still advertises built-in iCloud support. There is no clear way to decline permanently, so I now have to keep postponing a change I never requested. For professionals who use this app in meetings, the constant nagging is a real drain on productivity. If you want a quiet, dependable notetaker that keeps your notes where you choose, look elsewhere.

title.label: Great App Plagued by Untapped Potential and Poor Framework

content.label: Notability is a fantastic note taking software that is worth the optional buy-in for additional functionality. As a student who has used the app almost daily for 4 years, it is hard to imagine getting through college without it. Major features I like - you can import pdfs, images, and more into a note, and adjust your template in the same note. You can record audio that links to your writing strokes and navigate to where transcribed audio matches your notes. Depending on your tablet model, you can enable quick gestures/features that drastically speed up note taking, like double or triple taps to undo and redo strokes. You can also use Apple Pencil tapping gestures to swap tools if you have the right models. You can export pdfs and other file types, adjusting page count and more. Now, with all of that being said, as someone who has subscribed for years, this app has many issues that, frankly, have gone unaddressed by the Notability development team for too long. First and foremost, the biggest issue with this app is how it stores and loads your notes. If you have too little storage, or a bad iCloud sync occurs, your notes will be completely inaccessible. This has happened several times, and is well documented by other Notability users. Other small bugs have also persisted, like bad shape recognition for auto-drawing, poor UI such as file names at the top of notes being covered by drawing tools, and more. Furthermore, for every good feature there is with this app, there is a glaring gap of another. A primary example is there is no infinite canvas in the app. Still. Other lacking features like better file management/hierarchy are also frustrating (devs-give us sub-folders!), this includes the inability to name two notes the same, regardless of whether they exist in separate folders. Missing basic functionalities like these are frustrating when the dev-team appears more focused on improving AI note analysis. This brings me to my final issue with the app - only offering a subscription pricing model for a service that hasn’t fixed minor bugs, hasn’t offered greater note taking functionality, and poorly stores your files externally feels criminal. All-in-all, this is a great app that, unfortunately, has IMMENSE untapped potential, and a dev-team preoccupied with the wrong things. Do I recommend it? Yes. Do I find it frustrating and feel abandoned by the devs? Also yes.

This app is fine for taking notes. I purchased the premium version because I wanted to take advantage of the quizzes, tests, matching game, etc. However, if I have a 10 page note, it’ll only ask me questions from 3 of those pages. And it’s 80 questions! It even does the same thing if I have less pages, like 5 pages. Then it’ll only ask information from 1 or 2 pages. It never asks all or even half the information. I don’t think anyone should pay for this app until they adjust this. 10 questions based on a couple sentences is ridiculous. Just use this as a free note taking app to save paper. It was infinitely better spring semester 2026, idk why they butchered it for the paying customers. It also doesn’t update the quiz/test section if you do one of them and then add more to your notes after. You have to duplicate the note so it updates the quiz/test questions.

For the testing section: the fill in the blank portions are extremely confusing. A question is never asked, only a statement is made, and it looks like it should be true or false. This would be an example of something it asks: “There are different types of animals; cats are felines.” I would feel inclined to put true, but the answer would be something like mammal. And when I manage to guess what it’s asking of me, my answer is right, but either too specific or not specific enough or I put the acronym version. I wish there was a way to mark my answer as correct after being graded, so that it knows for next time that the answer I put is acceptable.

title.label: Okay app… cannot handle large PDFs without being a battery hog, but the simple UI is nice

content.label:
So I was about to stop using this app but it looks like it cannot handle huge PDFs without draining the battery. So if you have to annotate huge PDFs use a different app. But other than this, the UI is simple which I like. And I appreciate that they don’t change it every month like SOME other apps do (Goodnotes).

I would really like a scribble to erase feature that gives us the option to scribble with the pen over a portion of text to erase it. So many other apps at least give the option to do this, yet Notability STILL doesn’t. What also greatly annoys me is the lack of Apple Pencil hover support. This should be on notability by now (at least give us the option). And the squeeze to erase feature is beyond stupid to me. I already have the option to double tap my pencil to erase. Why do I need to have the same redundant option (that ergonomically makes zero sense) to simultaneously squeeze AND HOLD the Apple Pencil to erase? At least give us the option to squeeze for the tool palette like EVERY OTHER NOTES APP.

Needless to say, the lack of these features are embarrassing for an app that you have to pay a subscription for. What note takers want is 1) app reliability (include cloud note storage) 2) consistency and simplicity and 3) tools and functions that make our workflow easier.

More AI bloat gives us none of those things.

At the end, I will happily pay a subscription (within reasonable competitive pricing) if those 3 demands are met. I want features that make my like easier, and the AI stuff is great sure. But it’s time to pivot to reliability and consistency. If Notability meets these things, I will be very pleased.

title.label: Quality has went downhill over the past 4 years

content.label: Notability used to be my go to app for note taking on my iPad, but since the start of this semester, I’ve noticed it takes FOREVER to load notes. Each time I open the app, it’s like the app undownloaded all of my notes, and spends 5-6 minutes trying to fetch it from ICloud (even if no changes are made).  I normally download my class’s lectures before class to save time, because our professors tend to jump right in, but the new buffering time makes it so that I have to wait 5-10 minutes of class to start my notes. I have adequate storage 86/200 GB, and the app keeps informing me I need to have more storage (when that is obv not the case). I’ve done everything to make the app smoother but I’ve had no luck. I used to love this app, and paid premium (now I pay lite, to get me through this last semester in college), but if I’d known this app would go downhill like this, I wouldn’t have picked it to write all my notes (user since Freshman year of highschool, now a senior in college).
